title: Exchange a finite flat map and a completely decomposed etale family
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning it has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings. Let $\ell$ be prime, and let $f:Y\to X$ be finite locally free of constant positive rank $d$ prime to $\ell$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $(v_i:V_i\to Y)_i$ be a finite family of separated etale morphisms of finite type [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] that is completely decomposed: every $y\in Y$ has a point of some $V_i$ above it inducing an isomorphism of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field]. There exist a finite completely decomposed family of separated etale morphisms $u_j:U_j\to X$ of finite type, finite locally free surjections $c_j:Z_j\to U_j$ of constant positive ranks $d_j$ prime to $\ell$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism], indices $i(j)$, and $X$-morphisms $g_j:Z_j\to V_{i(j)}$ satisfying $f v_{i(j)}g_j=u_jc_j$. Neither $U_j$ nor $Z_j$ is asserted integral or reduced.

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.3, exchange assertion, printed pp. 30--31 (the printed W_j in Z_j -> W_j denotes U_j); finite affine-open refinement by Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. By [lem-pc-flf-properties], the finite algebra sheaf $f_*\mathcal O_Y$ is locally free of rank $d$. Choose an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ containing $x$ on which this sheaf is free, and the finiteness in [def-pc-finite-locally-free] makes its inverse image affine; write $Y_T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ free of rank $d$ over $A$. Apply [lem-per-ordinary-henselian-pointed-neighbourhood-limit] to $(T,x)$, obtaining a henselian local ring $H=\varinjlim_a A_a$ with residue field $\kappa(x)$ and affine etale pointed neighbourhoods $T_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$. Put $B_H=B\otimes_AH$. Tensoring the displayed basis gives $B_H\cong H^d$ as modules. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] to decompose $B_H=\prod_{t=1}^r C_t$ into nonzero finite henselian local $H$-algebras. Each $C_t$ is an $H$-module direct summand of $H^d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] it is locally finite free. In a local ring a family generating the unit ideal contains a unit, so one of that lemma's free principal localizations is $H$ itself: $C_t$ is free of some rank $e_t$.

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.3, exchange assertion, printed pp. 30--31 (the printed W_j in Z_j -> W_j denotes U_j); finite affine-open refinement by Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27.

proof.text: Each $C_t\ne0$ has $e_t>0$, and tensoring $B_H=\prod_t C_t$ with the residue field gives $d=\sum_t e_t$. If every $e_t$ were divisible by $\ell$, so would $d$ be. Choose $t$ with $\ell\nmid e_t$, put $C=C_t$, $e=e_t$, and let $q$ be its closed point. Its image $y\in Y_T\subseteq Y$ has a lift $w\in V_i$ for some $i$, with $\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(w)$, by the completely decomposed hypothesis. Choose an affine open $W\subseteq V_i\times_Y Y_T$ containing $w$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(q)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to W$ gives a rational point in the closed fibre of $W\times_{Y_T}\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. This explicitly supplies the residue-field lift needed next; it uses no assumption that $C$ is reduced or that its residue field equals $\kappa(x)$.

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.3, exchange assertion, printed pp. 30--31 (the printed W_j in Z_j -> W_j denotes U_j); finite affine-open refinement by Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27.

proof.text: Write $W=\operatorname{Spec}E$; its map to the affine $Y_T=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale by open restriction and etale composition/cancellation [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] the algebra $C\otimes_BE$ is etale over $C$. The preceding rational point defines a prime above the maximal ideal of $C$ with unchanged residue field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction], using the henselianity of $C$ given by the finite-product lemma in Step 1. The resulting retraction $C\otimes_BE\to C$ gives a section $s:\operatorname{Spec}C\to W$ over $Y_T$. Thus its composite to $Y_T$ factors as the inclusion of the open-and-closed component $\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B_H$ followed by the projection to $Y_T$.

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.3, exchange assertion, printed pp. 30--31 (the printed W_j in Z_j -> W_j denotes U_j); finite affine-open refinement by Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27.

proof.text: Let $b\in B_H$ be the idempotent selecting $C=bB_H$. The algebra $B_H=\varinjlim_a(B\otimes_A A_a)$ is a filtered colimit: tensoring a fixed algebra commutes with this colimit by the tensor-product universal property. Apply [lemma-nagata-filtered-colimit-finite-data] to lift $b$ and the equation $b^2=b$ to an idempotent $b_a\in B_a=B\otimes_AA_a$. Set $Z_a=\operatorname{Spec}(b_aB_a)\subseteq Y_{T_a}$. This is a clopen subscheme and is of finite presentation over $Y_{T_a}$, since $b_aB_a=B_a/(1-b_a)$. Its base change to $H$ is exactly $\operatorname{Spec}C$. The affine schemes $Y_{T_a}$ form an inverse system with affine transition maps; by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] its limit is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the colimit $\varinjlim_aB_a=B_H$ of their rings. Both $Z_a$ and $W\times_TT_a$ are of finite presentation over $Y_{T_a}$: for the latter, etale gives local finite presentation, and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] makes the affine ring map $B\to E$ finitely presented, hence so is its tensor base change by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Apply clause 2 of [thm-pd-spreading-out] over this system to descend $s$ to a morphism $Z_{a'}\to W\times_TT_{a'}$ over $Y_{T_{a'}}$ at a later index $a'$. Being a morphism over $Y_{T_{a'}}$ already gives the required commuting triangle with $V_i\to Y$.

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.3, exchange assertion, printed pp. 30--31 (the printed W_j in Z_j -> W_j denotes U_j); finite affine-open refinement by Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27.

proof.text: The map $Z_{a'}\to T_{a'}$ is locally of finite presentation: its clopen inclusion into $Y_{T_{a'}}$ has the one-relation presentation just displayed, and $Y_{T_{a'}}\to T_{a'}$ is the base change of the finite locally free map $Y_T\to T$; use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] for base change and composition. Here $Y_T\to T$ is of finite presentation, since [def-pc-finite-locally-free] gives local finite presentation and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] applied to its affine source and target makes $A\to B$ finitely presented. All composition and base-change claims here are therefore applications of the cited ring-map theorem to these affine charts. Its base change to $H$ is $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}H$, finite locally free of constant rank $e$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum] and its chosen $e$-element basis. All schemes in this application are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The system $T_a$, $a\ge a'$, has limit $\operatorname{Spec}H$ by the last clause of [lem-per-ordinary-henselian-pointed-neighbourhood-limit]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free] to the fixed model $Z_{a'}\to T_{a'}$ and pass to a later stage $a''$ where it is finite locally free of constant rank $e$. The map to $V_i$ persists under base change.

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.3, exchange assertion, printed pp. 30--31 (the printed W_j in Z_j -> W_j denotes U_j); finite affine-open refinement by Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27.

proof.text: The neighbourhood construction gives a separated etale map $T_{a''}\to T$ of finite presentation, hence of finite type. For the open inclusion $j:T\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] applied to every affine open $P\subseteq X$ shows that $P\cap T$ is quasi-compact. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact, so [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes it finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] and [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $u_x:T_{a''}\to T\hookrightarrow X$ is etale and finite type. It is separated: since $j$ is a monomorphism, $T_{a''}\times_XT_{a''}=T_{a''}\times_TT_{a''}$, and the diagonal is the closed immersion of the separated map $T_{a''}\to T$. The designated point over $x$ still has residue field $\kappa(x)$.

source.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.3, exchange assertion, printed pp. 30--31 (the printed W_j in Z_j -> W_j denotes U_j); finite affine-open refinement by Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27.

proof.text: Write $Z_x=Z_{a''}$ and $c_x:Z_x\to T_{a''}$. It is surjective: over any point of $T_{a''}$ its fibre algebra has positive dimension $e$, hence is a nonzero finite-dimensional algebra over a field and has a maximal ideal, which gives a point of that fibre. Thus $c_x$ is a finite locally free surjection of positive rank prime to $\ell$, with a map $g_x:Z_x\to V_i$ satisfying $fv_i g_x=u_xc_x$. Carry this construction out for each $x$. The resulting family $(u_x)_x$ is completely decomposed because its designated lift at $x$ has exactly $\kappa(x)$. Apply [lem-per-completely-decomposed-etale-finite-subcover] to retain a finite subfamily, with the corresponding $Z_x,c_x,g_x$ and indices $i$. This gives all the required data. If $X$ is empty, the empty family already satisfies every assertion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q96-fdf37bb8b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 7 steps and both new nodes in full, together with every cited statement. Sources read: ILO II 2.1.1, 2.2.2–2.2.4 and the 3.2.3 exchange sketch (printed pp. 26–31), and Stacks 04GN lemma-henselization with its proof. The item statement is unchanged and matches the ILO exchange in finite form; no SGA is cited. Step 1 is correct: f_*O_Y is free on an affine T, B_H=∏C_t splits into henselian local factors (04GH node), and each C_t is free because a direct summand over a local ring becomes free after localizing at one f_i, which is a unit. Step 2 is correctly marked elementary: d=Σe_t over κ(x), so some e_t is prime to ℓ, and the κ(q)-point of W×_{Y_T}Spec C has residue field κ(q). Step 3 checks the hypotheses of the henselian étale retraction (C henselian, prime with trivial residue extension). Step 4 lifts b to a genuine idempotent, Z_a and W×_T T_a are of finite presentation, and 01ZM(2) gives a morphism over Y_{T_a'}, so f v g = u c holds. Step 5: 06AC applies (everything affine, f_0 locally of finite presentation) and gives constant degree e. Step 6: j is quasi-compact because X is Noetherian, finite type follows, and separatedness holds because j is a monomorphism. Step 7: positive rank gives surjectivity, and the subcover node gives a finite family; empty X is fine. New node lem-per-ordinary-henselian-pointed-neighbourhood-limit is true (04GN applied to A_p, descended along A_g; points κ(x)⊆κ(x_a)⊆κ(H); cofinal directed set; 01YW). It is not a duplicate: the existing etale-triples nodes all carry IsSepClosure, and pair-henselization and prime-ind-etale give no pointed A-system. New node lem-per-completely-decomposed-etale-finite-subcover is true by ILO 2.2.4 (ind-constructible cd loci, X_cons compact) and is not a duplicate. Neither new node restates an item clause. FIX (C1): Step 4 identified lim Y_{T_a}=Spec B_H only 'by the tensor universal property'; it now cites lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition (01YW), which is added to proof_deps and tool_uses. Step 5 now cites the limit clause of the new neighbourhood node for lim T_a=Spec H, which 06AC requires. No other changes.
